what_it_does: A Coarse-Grained Reconfigurable Array (CGRA) is a chip whose processing units can be rewired in software to run different programs efficiently — sitting between a fixed chip (like a GPU) and a fully custom chip. To use a CGRA well, a compiler must figure out how to map each step of a program (especially loops) onto the chip's grid of units, which is a combinatorially hard search problem. GPS tackles this with a two-stage approach: first it uses a mathematical solver (Integer Linear Programming, which finds the best assignment given formal rules) to get an initial rough layout, then a graph neural network (an AI model that reasons over graph-structured data, here the program's dependency graph) refines and prunes the search space. This combination significantly reduces search time while improving the quality of the final mapping.
